item.title: Jamal Musiala unfazed by controversy per report
item.description: (Photo by Stefan Matzke - sampics/Getty Images) | Getty Images There is plenty of noise surrounding Jamal Musiala right now, but the latest reporting suggests that, at least for the moment, the Bayern Munich star is not letting it distract him from his priorities. According to Fabrizio Romano (via @iMiaSanMia ), Musiala remains fully committed to Bayern Munich, wants to fight his way back to his best level, and is focused on giving everything he can for the club. His contract extension was not simply about securing a lucrative payday, but about his genuine affection for Bayern and his desire to continue there. That is an important distinction amid the growing controversy surrounding Musiala’s situation, his recovery, and the broader conversations about where things stand between the player and the club. There is no indication that Musiala is actively looking for an exit today. However, Romano’s report does leave the door open to a different conversation down the road. If the situation at Bayern Munich continues to deteriorate or fails to improve to Musiala’s satisfaction, a potential departure could eventually be considered. For now, Musiala wants to fight, recover, and succeed at Bayern. The longer-term outlook, however, may depend on how the club navigates the situation from here. Join the conversation! item.title: Surprise AL East team pushes Mets to make Tarik Skubal richest pitcher in MLB history
item.description: The New York Mets have their ace for nearly the next decade. According to multiple reports, the Mets have agreed to a nine-year deal with left-hander Tarik Skubal worth $450 million. The deal does not include any opt-outs and includes $30 million in deferrals, per Joel Sherman of the New York Post . The deal is easily the richest contract in MLB history handed out to a pitcher, excluding two-way superstar Shohei Ohtani, surpassing Yoshinobu Yamamoto’s deal which was for 12 years and $325 million. MORE: Mets to sign 22-year-old outfielder to $95 million contract; are they done? Skubal is one of the best pitchers the league has ever seen. The 30-year-old owned a 2.72 ERA last year, collecting 186 strikeouts in 158 2/3 innings split between the Los Angeles Dodgers and Detroit Tigers. He has one of the most impressive resumes in baseball, winning the AL Triple Crown for pitching and earning two All-Star selections and a Cy Young Award. Oct 7, 2026; Cumberland, Georgia, USA; Los Angeles Dodgers pitcher Tarik Skubal (29) looks on before game four against the Atlanta Braves in the NLDS for the 2026 MLB Playoffs at Truist Park. Mandatory Credit: Brett Davis-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters) Mets forced to outbit surprise AL East club Still, the offer for Skubal was an expensive one. While it was clear why the Mets did it, it was unclear who was driving the price so high. One of the other bidders for Skubal, the Dodgers, did not even make an offer, according to Alden Gonzalez of ESPN . The reasoning for why they had to pay so much came out hours after the deal was reported. According to Mitch Bannon of The Athletic , the Toronto Blue Jays made an offer above $400 million over nine years. While the deal was millions short of New York’s, the Blue Jays have had more postseason success than the Mets, reaching the World Series in 2025, and have a more complete team. That is part of the reason why the Mets had to pay what they did to land Skubal in Queens. The #BlueJays ’ offer to Skubal was 9 years, just over $400 million, per sources. Would’ve set pitching contract records and been the 2nd biggest Jays contract. But, as many assumed all along, Mets weren’t to be beat. Updated with the new info here: https://t.co/gPxXODdQLN — Mitch Bannon (@MitchBannon) November 23, 2026 The Mets fell well short of expectations in 2026. With Skubal joining the club for the 2027 season and beyond, they certainly have a better chance of making the postseason. — Enjoy free coverage of the top news & trending stories with The Big Lead Newsletter —

item.title: Cam Skattebo breaks celebration promise less than 1 week after making it
item.description: NFL players are known for their signature celebrations, but sometimes a memorable moment can lead to a change of heart. Cam Skattebo recently made it clear he was done with a risky celebration after seeing Aidan Hutchinson suffer a serious injury, only for that decision to apparently last less than a week. MORE: Patrick Mahomes gives very direct, funny answer when asked about his recent success Skattebo said he was done with backflips Aug 22, 2026; Miami Gardens, Florida, USA; New York Giants running back Cam Skattebo (44) warms up prior to a preseason game against the Miami Dolphins at Hard Rock Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Rich Storry-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters) After watching Aidan Hutchinson suffer a season-ending knee injury while celebrating a sack, Cam Skattebo said he was done with his signature backflip celebration. The Giants running back made it clear he didn’t want to risk suffering a similar injury, saying he was serious about ending the celebration. Cam Skattebo doesn’t want to do backflip TD celebration anymore after seeing Aidan Hutchinson injury: "I’m done flipping, just for that reason. It’s hard to see. Don’t want it to happen to me … Mentally, I’m like: Fuck it. I’m not doing that shit. That shit ain’t going to happen to me." Skattebo added later on in the interview: "I’m sure I’ll do it at some point, if we go to the playoffs or something." (via @DarrylSlater) — Underdog NFL (@UnderdogNFL) November 19, 2026 “It’s hard to see,” Skattebo said after seeing Hutchinson’s injury. “Mentally, I’m like, ‘I’m not doing that. That ain’t going to happen to me.'” Skattebo even suggested the celebration could be retired for good, although he left open the possibility of bringing it back if the Giants reached the playoffs. Skattebo already back to his signature celebration Nov 12, 2026; East Rutherford, New Jersey, USA; New York Giants running back Cam Skattebo (44) celebrates after scoring a touchdown during the first half against the Washington Commanders at MetLife Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Vincent Carchietta-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters) Apparently, Skattebo didn’t stick to that promise for very long. Less than a week after announcing he was done with the backflip, the Giants running back was back performing his signature celebration, creating a funny turnaround after his recent comments about retiring the move. Considering how emphatic Skattebo was about avoiding the celebration after Hutchinson’s injury, the quick return is sure to get plenty of attention from NFL fans. item.description: Pittsburgh Steelers WR DK Metcalf gets into a skirmish with Philadelphia Eagles players during a 19-16 loss on Sunday, Nov. 22, 2026. -- Ed Thompson / Steelers Now PHILADELPHIA — The noise around DK Metcalf has been swelling for weeks. The receiver’s abbreviated performance during a 19-16 road loss to the Philadelphia Eagles on Sunday did nothing to silence to it. The 6-foot-4 star wideout had one catch for two yards on the day, marking the second time in three games that Metcalf was limited to a single grab, enough cause on its own for fans of Mike McCarthy’s team to get riled up. Add to that the fact that Metcalf was ejected in the third quarter for mixing it up with Eagles defensive back Cooper DeJean, and the angst is at an all-time high. Denver Broncos insider Benjamin Allbright wrote that a league source told him Metcalf, “considered a repeat offender,” could be suspended and miss Friday’s home matchup with Sean Payton’s team. DK Metcalf has been ejected for unsportsmanlike conduct. Metcalf was ejected after two personal fouls. (📺 CBS) pic.twitter.com/f1OE50Fn6I — NFL on ESPN (@ESPNNFL) November 22, 2026 No stranger to penalties and fines, Metcalf has been the subject of unwanted headlines on a handful of occasions since entering the NFL in 2019. During his third season with the Seattle Seahawks, Metcalf was tossed late from a 2021 loss to the Green Bay Packers for gripping Henry Black’s face mask and shoving Rasul Douglas in his. In 2023 , Metcalf was ejected late in the final frame of a road setback against the San Francisco 49ers, suplexing Niners linebacker Fred Warner after an interception and getting up and grabbing him by the face mask with both hands after Warner bowled into him on the ground. The confrontation led to a scuffle between both teams. ‘We need him’ Fans underline the four-year, $132 million contract the Steelers gave Metcalf after trading for him two offseasons ago. He hasn’t lived up to the expectations that come with the deal, and Pittsburgh could’ve gotten out of future guarantees after his incident with a fan in Detroit a campaign ago, another subject of ire and example of Metcalf not keeping his cool. The Steelers demonstrated a measure of trust by not doing so, however, even after he was suspended the final two games of the regular season and Pittsburgh had to squeak into the playoffs via a last-second field goal miss in the finale. item.title: Steelers’ updated playoff odds after disastrous loss to Eagles
item.description: Mandatory Credit: Eric Hartline-Imagn Images Steelers’ updated playoff odds after disastrous loss to Eagles appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Pittsburgh Steelers went into their bye week with a 6-2 record and an excellent chance to win the AFC North title. They also fell short against the Eagles, dropping a Week 11 19-16 decision in Philadelphia. The Steelers are tied for second in the AFC North with the Cleveland Browns. Both teams have 6-4 records. Rodgers got little support from the Steelers running game and he was forced to put the ball in the air 44 times. He completed 30 passes for 227 yards, but that average of 5.2 yards per pass was indicative of an offense that has problems sustaining drives. The two losses to the Bengals and the Eagles were both road games. The Steelers return home Friday to host the Denver Broncos and they will also host the Houston Texans in Week 13. item.title: Mizzou Wrestling Takes Keystone Classic Behind Three Individual Titles
item.description: No. 9 Mizzou wrestling made a statement at the Keystone Classic on Sunday, claiming the team championship with 179.5 points at The Palestra in Philadelphia. The Tigers finished 11 points ahead of No. 3 Nebraska, which placed second, to secure the tournament title. Mizzou was led by three individual champions in Gage Walker (133lbs), Seth Mendoza (149lbs) and Aeoden Sinclair (184lbs). Sinclair earned Outstanding Wrestler honors after a dominant performance that saw him win all five of his matches, including four bonus-point victories. Mizzou’s 19 competitors combined for a 50-24 record, with 12 wrestlers finishing among the tournament’s top six. The Tigers also recorded 27 bonus-point victories, including 13 technical falls and five pins. All rankings are according to InterMat 125 No. 31 Mack Mauger led Mizzou at 125lbs, finishing as the tournament runner-up with a 3-1 record. Mauger opened with a 14-5 major decision over Penn’s Marius Garcia before earning a 4-2 decision against Nebraska’s Kael Lauridsen in the quarterfinals. He followed that with a 4-1 semifinal victory over Penn’s No. 10 Max Ghallager to advance to the championship match. Mauger ultimately fell 8-3 to Rutgers’ No. 14 Anthony Knox, settling for second place. Jason Hampton also competed at the weight, finishing 1-2. 133 No. 9 Gage Walker captured Mizzou’s first individual championship of the day, going 4-0 to take first place at 133lbs. Walker opened with a 12-3 major decision before recording a 15-0 technical fall in the quarterfinals. He then earned a 6-4 decision over Virginia Tech’s Nicholas Garcia to reach the finals. Walker capped his performance with a 10-1 major decision over Michigan State’s Caleb Weiand. Teammate Zion Borge also reached the podium, finishing fifth with a 4-1 record. 141 No. 12 Zan Fugitt secured a third-place finish at 141lbs, going 3-1 throughout the tournament. Fugitt opened with a pin before adding a 17-2 technical fall in the quarterfinals. After falling 4-3 to Nebraska’s Omar Ayoub in the semifinals, Fugitt bounced back with a 5-1 decision over Harvard’s No. 32 Coleman Nogle in the third-place match. Easton Hilton finished fifth with a 5-1 record, while Yandel Morales went 1-2. 149 No. 12 Seth Mendoza earned Mizzou’s second individual championship, finishing 4-0 at 149lbs. Mendoza began his tournament with a 19-4 technical fall over Virginia Tech’s Walker Turley before recording an 18-3 technical fall against Nebraska’s Scott Robertson. He advanced to the finals with a pin over Lock Haven’s No. 17 Lucas Kapusta in just 2:34. In the championship match, Mendoza edged Penn’s No. 7 Cross Wasilewski, 2-1, to claim the title. Demetri Carrera also competed at the weight, finishing 0-2. 157 Kollin Rath earned a runner-up finish at 157lbs, putting together a 3-1 tournament record. Rath opened with a 9-1 major decision over Michigan State’s No. 33 Darius Marines before earning narrow decisions over Rutgers’ No. 20 Conner Harer and Penn’s No. 15 Jude Swisher

item.title: Colts-Giants opening odds: A fresh start
item.description: PHILADELPHIA, PA - NOVEMBER 08: A detailed view of the Giants helmet is shown during the game between the Philadelphia Eagles and New York Giants on November 8th, 2026 at Lincoln Financial Field in Philadelphia, PA. (Photo by Terence Lewis/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Indianapolis Colts have continued to look different as the season has progressed. This Sunday against the Giants, they will look incredibly different. At the game’s most important position, the Colts will start a new quarterback. Daniel Jones is out. Anthony Richardson is in. Despite the quarterback change, FanDuel Sportsbook sees more of the same as the Colts are 7-point underdogs. The money line comes in at +290 and the over/under is 42.5. The Colts are coming off another dreadful performance against the Texans. Thursday marked a fateful day for Jones as it was the straw that broke the camel’s back. The season’s failure cannot be blamed on Jones alone, but his play has had a lot to do with it. A swirl of rumors as the reason for his departure lingers over the franchise. The team will turn to Richardson, but if the rest of the offense that played in Houston shows up on Sunday, it won’t matter much. The Giants have been one of the surprises this year in the NFL. At 5-3-1, they are leading the NFC East. That division isn’t great, but beating the Jaguars goes a long way to providing them legitimacy. The Giants took the lead late in the first quarter and never looked back. J.J. McCarthy is the new man in town and looking to make a statement after being traded by the Vikings. Expect the Giants to put up a massive fight. The Colts’ season is done, but that doesn’t mean there is nothing to play for. Anthony Richardson and others up and down the roster are auditioning for next year either with the Colts or elsewhere. These players are professionals. Winning against the Giants would be a great step in the right direction. Let’s see if the Colts can get it done.

item.title: Bills’ Josh Allen admits he’s ‘a little ticked off’ despite crushing Dolphins to get to 9-1
item.description: Mark Konezny-Imagn Images Bills’ Josh Allen admits he’s ‘a little ticked off’ despite crushing Dolphins to get to 9-1 appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Josh Allen kept things in perspective as he expected a stronger performance in the Buffalo Bills’ 26-9 win over the Miami Dolphins on Sunday afternoon. Allen has been playing in the NFL since 2018, going through his ninth season with the Bills. He shines as one of the best players in the entire league, looking to finally lead Buffalo to a Super Bowl after multiple heartbreaks in the playoffs. Buffalo has one of the best records in the league, and they kept that going by beating Miami at home. However, Allen and the squad didn’t have a dominant day against their division rival. It was noticeable that even the star quarterback himself noted that aspect following the win. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) “That’s division football. Got a lot of things to clean up. It’s very much a luxury to sit here, be 9-1 and be a little ticked off about how you played. So we got a lot of things to clean up. Happy we got the win. Got a short week on Thursday night against a really good team coming up, so we got to put this one behind us, learn from it, and look forward,” Allen said on the CBS broadcast. "It's very much a luxury to sit here, be 9-1 and be a little ticked off about how you played." Josh Allen happy to get a win, but telling @AKinkhabwala the @BuffaloBills are far from satisfied pic.twitter.com/ogTj7dEXEe — NFL on CBS 🏈 (@NFLonCBS) November 22, 2026 How Josh Allen, Bills played against Dolphins The Bills are in firm position to clinch a playoff spot, especially in the top four as they lead over the AFC East in convincing fashion. Beating the Dolphins only pushes them in that direction. Josh Allen didn’t have a perfect day as he made some mistakes. He completed 27 out of 45 passes for 304 yards and a touchdown and two interceptions. James Cook dominated with his activity on the ground. He racked up 22 carries for 89 yards and a touchdown. Khalil Shakir led receivers with 101 yards on five catches, while DJ Moore caught eight passes for 91 yards and a touchdown. The Bills do indeed have a short break as they will be active on Thanksgiving week, remaining at home. They host the Kansas City Chiefs in Week 12 as kickoff commences on Nov. 26 at 8:20 p.m. ET. item.title: Liverpool thrash 10-man Man Utd in Pochettino's first match
item.description: Rio Ngumoha shone in Liverpool's thrashing of 10-man Manchester United (Paul ELLIS) Mauricio Pochettino endured a nightmare start as Manchester United manager with a 4-0 defeat at Liverpool that left the Red Devils still rooted in the Premier League relegation zone. United never recovered from Leny Yoro's controversial red card after just eight minutes as Dominik Szoboszlai and Florian Wirtz quickly made Liverpool's man advantage count. Teenager Rio Ngumoha rounded off a stunning individual with Liverpool's third before Victor Munoz completed the rout. Defeat leaves United second bottom of the table and gave Pochettino an early indication of the huge job he has ahead to restore the 20-time English champions to their former glories. "We feel pain for that defeat, but we need to keep the head up and translate that anger to an energy to start to work from tomorrow for the next game," said Pochettino, who was furious at the decision to dismiss Yoro. "I need to defend my club and say what I feel. I feel like that was an action that everyone who plays football can see was clearly not a red card.". Liverpool climb into the top four and within seven points of leaders Arsenal to rekindle faint hopes of challenging for the title. "We could have scored more," said Liverpool boss Andoni Iraola. "In other games you will remember those chances, but today we've controlled the game and everything was happening around the (United) box." Pochettino answered United's call after Michael Carrick was sacked last week after winning just one of the Red Devils' first 10 league games in charge. The Argentine has been linked with a move to Old Trafford for a decade, but failed to make a strong first impression on the United fans. - Europe's worst defence - Pochettino's bold team selection backfired with the centre-back pairing of Matthijs de Ligt and Yoro at fault for the game's decisive moment. De Ligt, on his first Premier League start for nearly a year, let a long ball down the middle and go and allowed Alexander Isak to bear down on goal. The Swedish striker took a heavy touch before he was clipped by Yoro, but referee Sam Barrott still deemed the French defender had denied a clear goalscoring opportunity and produced a red card. Szoboszlai rubbed salt into United wounds by drilling home the resulting free-kick from the edge of the box. Moments later Ngumoha skipped past Diogo Dalot and crossed for Wirtz to hook a shot in off the underside of the bar. Having relegated Harry Maguire to the bench, Pochettino was forced to turn to the veteran centre-back just 22 minutes in to try and stem the bleeding. United lost 7-0 at Anfield three years ago and a switch to a back five helped avoid similar damage, albeit with the help of some wayward Liverpool finishing. Maguire made a brilliant block to deny Isak a third goal just before half-time. Bradley Barcola and Isak were guilty of wasting huge chances early in the second half. item.title: Patriots vs. Chargers Opening Odds: Bolts slight favorite in Week 12
item.description: FOXBOROUGH, MASSACHUSETTS - JANUARY 11: Rhamondre Stevenson #38 of the New England Patriots carries the ball defended by Troy Dye #43 of the Los Angeles Chargers during the third quarter of the AFC Wild Card Playoff game at Gillette Stadium on January 11, 2026 in Foxborough, Massachusetts. (Photo by Sarah Stier/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Los Angeles Chargers are 1-9 after falling to the New York Jets at home in Week 11. Now the Chargers will have a chance to go up against the New England Patriots at home in Week 12. The Patriots are coming off their bye week, which was much needed after their Week 10 loss against the Detroit Lions in Munich, where they lost Drake Maye to an ankle injury that could keep him out for the rest of the year. This means Tommy DeVito is set to start for the Pats against the Chargers, which gives Los Angeles a chance to pull out its second win of the season. The Bolts entered this week as 1.5-point favorites, per FanDuel Sportsbook . The over/under is currently set at 37.5 points. The Chargers killed some of their momentum after beating the Baltimore Ravens on Monday Night Football, with a loss against the New York Jets. The Chargers trailed 17-3 with 3 minutes to go in the second quarter, forcing them to mount a comeback. While Justin Herbert ran for a touchdown as time expired in the first half and completed two touchdowns to Ladd McConkey in the fourth quarter, they ultimately fell short by a field goal against the Jets. Herbert entered the league’s concussion protocol following the game, and his status is up in the air for the contest against the Patriots. item.title: RSM Classic Issues Apology After Disappointing PGA Tour Ticket Decision
item.description: | Source: Lastwordonsports.com - Ajayi Segun The RSM Classic has issued an apology to fans after its decision to turn away Saturday ticket holders from Sunday’s rescheduled third round. The tournament’s organizers acknowledged the disappointment caused by the decision and explained why they could not allow additional spectators into the grounds. The Davis Love Foundation shared a statement on the RSM Classic’s official X page on Sunday, addressing the concerns surrounding the ticket arrangements. The organization said the safety of spectators and volunteers remained its priority after heavy rainfall left the tournament grounds saturated. The decision means fans who purchased Saturday tickets will miss the rescheduled third round, while Monday’s final round will also take place without spectators. The foundation has now explained why it could not make different arrangements for those affected. The organization also addressed the decision to prevent fans from attending Monday’s final round. Although the tournament had already announced that the grounds would be closed to the public, the foundation provided further explanation for the arrangement. “Regarding Monday’s final round, limited volunteer support and related infrastructure prevent us from making tickets available to the public,” the statement added. The weather disruption forced the PGA Tour to move the third round from Saturday to Sunday and the final round from Sunday to Monday. However, the foundation said the lack of volunteer support and the infrastructure needed to accommodate spectators meant it could not open the grounds for Monday’s play. item.title: Rams release 1st injury report for Week 12
item.description: (Photo by Luke Hales/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Los Angeles Rams have injuries stacking up at the wide receiver position, with both Davante Adams and Puka Nacua on the injured reserve. With that being said, there was some talk of Adams potentially returning from his hamstring injury for the Rams’ Thanksgiving Eve matchup against the Green Bay Packers. It does not appear that Adams will be returning for action this week. First of all, Adams’ practice window has not opened up, so he remains on the injured reserve to start the week. The limited participants were offensive lineman Steve Avila (hamstring, usually the team’s starting left guard), safety Kam Curl (toe), center Coleman Shelton (hamstring) and tight end Terrance Ferguson (ankle/hamstring). item.title: 8 Winners & Losers as NY Mets Win Tarik Skubal Sweepstakes, Including Blue Jays

The Mets are giving the two-time Cy Young Award winner a nine-year contract worth $450 million . But even if he doesn’t, he will still go down in history — at least for a little while — as the highest-paid pitcher the sport has ever had. That can’t be taken away until that number is broken, and with a salary cap likely coming to MLB in 2027 or soon after, that may never happen. item.title: FC Cincinnati deliver result of the playoffs with upset win over Nashville
item.description: FC Cincinnati deliver result of the playoffs with upset win over Nashville By Ben Steiner Short rest, raucous atmosphere, Supporters' Shield winners – none of that mattered for FC Cincinnati . In front of a sold-out crowd, FC Cincinnati secured a feat no other team could at GEODIS Park in 2026: A win. Thanks to a 7th-minute own goal by Nashville SC 's Patrick Yazbek , the Orange & Blue held on to secure a 1-0 win to open their Round One Best-of-3 series in the Audi 2026 MLS Cup Playoffs on Sunday. Just three days after a road win over Orlando City in the Wild Card, Cincinnati brought back shades of Atlanta United in 2024, when the Five Stripes advanced past Supporters’ Shield-winning, points-record-breaking Inter Miami . Cincinnati are now one win away from shockingly advancing to the Eastern Conference Semifinals. “If I were to flip the script. I would say we should have won the game,” head coach Pat Noonan said. “That's how I assessed it, and that's okay. That's the reality of how the game played out, and the result doesn't always match the performance. So yes, we're fortunate in how the own goal happened.” Stellar Celentano Cincinnati bunkered down as the game wore on, taking off talismanic midfielder Evander in the 67th minute to fortify their defense. Despite the eventual favorable scoreline, it wasn’t a smooth ride. The visitors weathered immense pressure throughout, leaning on a stellar performance from star goalkeeper Roman Celentano . Celentano, who had been benched in favor of Evan Louro earlier this year, stepped up with six stops, including a sprawling save after a headed chance from Sam Surridge . “[The win against] Orlando doesn’t matter. All that mattered was moving on and getting the job done tonight, and we did that,” Celentano told Apple TV. “I feel like we were just up against it the whole time. Nashville is the best team in the league for a reason, but tonight they were just putting us in. We had to just find a way to sit deep, defend the moments, and get them on the counter.” “I thought everyone just played for the badge and played with their hearts tonight. Everyone played great. Everyone gave everything, and that's why we got the win.” Player of the Match: Roman Celentano | Round One, Game One Work still to do Although Sunday’s win was special, there’s work to be done for Cincinnati. Despite being a No. 9 seed, Cincinnati can eliminate the Supporters’ Shield winners at home on Saturday (6:30 pm ET | Apple TV ), while Nashville will need a road win to force a Game 3 back at GEODIS Park. item.title: 4-star RB Yoshawn Hudson commits to Tulane
item.description: Tulane has pulled off a significant recruiting win, landing a commitment from four-star running back Yoshawn Hudson . The playmaker out of Winona (Miss.) recently backed off his commitment to Mississippi State , reopening his recruitment with Signing Day approaching. It didn’t take long for the Green Wave to emerge as his choice. Hudson made an official visit to Tulane over the weekend, and the trip helped seal the deal. “Tulane was hitting me up when I was committed to State, so they have always been there,” Hudson told Rivals. That consistency proved important. Hudson was familiar with Tulane before his official visit. He had already spent time on campus earlier in the recruiting process and developed relationships with the coaching staff. Those early connections gave Tulane a foundation to build on when Hudson reopened his recruitment. The Green Wave didn’t have to introduce themselves to the four-star running back. They had already established interest, and Hudson knew what the program had to offer. When it came time to make his decision, Hudson said, “The coaches, they believed in me. They want to help me develop. The people there are great too.” The experience on the official visit gave him peace. “The vibe was great. Me and my family had a great time. “I like Coach Hall too. He’s a great coach, and he’s going to get the ball to his backs.”

item.title: Jaguars fall to Giants 23-18 as Trevor Lawrence, offense struggles
item.description: Not good enough. The Jacksonville Jaguars (7-3) entered Sunday's matchup against the New York Giants (6-3-1) with plenty of momentum after a three-game winning streak. All of it was pushed aside from the outset, as they fell 23-18. The loss gives Jacksonville their third on the year, and while they still lead the AFC South, it could come back to bite them at the end of the season when playoff seeding is finalized. Against a fellow division leader, the Jaguars looked like the little brother in the relationship. And quarterback Trevor Lawrence regressed mightily, looking shaken by New York's pass rush early — too little, too late. FINAL RECAP: Jaguars lose to Giants in Week 11 Jacksonville's chances of mounting a comeback against New York were quickly dashed after a review determined receiver Parker Washington did not complete a catch in the back of the end zone for a touchdown in the fourth quarter. The score would have put Jacksonville within seven points with about 13 minutes left in the contest. The controversial call forced the Jaguars to kick a field goal, cutting New York's lead to 11 points after Cam Little's third made field goal of the day. Giants pressure disrupts Trevor Lawrence, Jaguars offense Jacksonville experienced its worst start to a game Sunday, at least offensively. The Jaguars mustered just six points on their first four drives, totaling 59 net yards. On the team's third drive, Lawrence threw an ill-advised pass into the area where receiver Parker Washington was. Lawrence also committed an illegal forward pass penalty earlier in the contest. In that span, Lawrence had completed 7 of 13 passes for 78 yards and an interception. The offense also committed five penalties during that time, including two false starts, a delay of game, an illegal forward pass and an illegal formation foul. The slew of penalties came just one week after the Jaguars committed just two flags against the Titans. A poor offensive showcase early in the game helped create the team's 11-point second-quarter deficit. It marked the largest deficit the Jaguars have faced since Week 6 against the Houston Texans, when the team trailed 24-14 at one point. Jacksonville trailed 20-6 at halftime. Lawrence finished the first half completing 10 of 16 passes for 106 yards and an interception. He was sacked three times and hit five times in the first half. Despite entering the red zone twice in the first half, Jacksonville managed just six points (two field goals). Jacksonville didn't get better once the second half began. The Jaguars scored nine points in the second half, including a late fourth-quarter touchdown to Brian Thomas Jr. Jaguars converted 17% (1 of 6) in the red zone against New York. Entering the game, the Giants' defense was giving up a touchdown on 80% of teams' red-zone trips. item.title: How Columbus Crew turned it all around to set up MLS playoff showdown vs. Messi
item.description: It wasn’t working. Issa Tall had to admit that. Well, he didn’t really have to. The results told the story for him. The Columbus Crew didn’t win in its first five MLS matches. By the World Cup break, 15 games in, they’d only added two more. There needed to be changes, and they needed to be big. The Crew general manager moved quickly. In May, he fired coach Henrik Rydström, his first coaching hire as the Crew’s chief soccer officer, though he was quick to point out he was involved with previous hires including bringing in Wilfried Nancy. He spent big in the summer, revamping the Crew’s attack and adding pieces while bidding farewell to some regulars. Ten players arrived, and eight went out. It worked. The Crew turned the boat around, going from worst in the Eastern Conference to closing the season on a six-game win streak and having won eight of their last nine. That was enough not only to jump out of Thursday’s wild card match but to set up a First Round playoff series with Inter Miami, the reigning champion led by Lionel Messi. They also pushed to the U.S. Open Cup final, falling to St. Louis City in a penalty shootout. All of it led Tall to believe he made the right decisions, moving on quickly from the coach he thought was the right man for the job. “Some people could’ve waited the full year. Maybe it would’ve been safer, but that’s not me. That’s not us as a club. That’s not even the way we play!” Tall told USA TODAY Sports ahead of the playoffs. “You see how we are bold and are not afraid of taking risk. At the end of the day, it wasn’t even a risk necessarily. It was necessary for our players, for our club as a whole and I think ultimately we made the right decision to do it at that time.” Tall still stands by Rydström as a good coach, something he’s proving while leading Hammarby in Sweden which currently sits atop of the table after running off five consecutive wins. But he wasn’t the right fit for the Crew in the post-Nancy era. The Crew turned to Courtois, a former Crew academy and MLS Next Pro coach who continued the idea first expressed on the field so successfully by Nancy’s teams. The squad might not have been the entirely right squad, either. Tall turned to a scouting network led by Mark Nichols, bringing in a proven MLS veteran in Santi Rodriguez, Chile national team forward Gonzalo Tapia, securing a loan deal for Moroccan winger Anass Zaroury and signing designated player Brais Mendez, a Spanish attacker whose arrival from Real Sociedad brought to mind that of Cucho Hernandez. While Mendez is at a different stage of his carer than Hernandez was, he turned into a star in Columbus, showing his full potential in MLS after frustrating stints with Watford and loans in Huseca, Mallorca and Getafe. item.title: Gotham FC’s title defense comes to crushing end in semifinal loss after venue change
item.description: They came by car, by the special-event X80 bus, by bike if they were feeling sporty. They came in layers, in beanies and scarves, with Gotham’s black-and-sky-blue colors on top. They came on behalf of those who couldn’t come, capacity being reduced at this impromptu change of venue, each one trying to make noise for five. Gotham FC forward Sam Kerr (20) competes for the ball against Kansas City Current defender Gabrielle Robinson (24) on Sunday, Nov. 15, 2026, in New York City. IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect They came with some measure of outrage — these home-field shenanigans would never happen in men’s sports — while their better angels told them to come in joy, in celebration, everyone watching women’s sports. And then, 25 miles and 20,000 seats removed from their regular destination at New Jersey’s Sports Illustrated Stadium, huddled in the bleachers by a blue track ringing an immaculate pitch at Icahn Stadium on Randall’s Island, in the shadow of the old Psychiatric Center and with the light fading over the Costco across the river, 5,000 devoted souls Sunday afternoon watched Gotham’s NWSL title defense end in a 2-1 semifinal loss to the Kansas City Current. “We lost today because we weren’t the better team,” Gotham winger and oracle Midge Purce said. “That being said, I would say it’s inexcusable. It’s not what you want in a professional league. It’s not what you want for women who are progressing in the United States and supposed to be one of the best leagues in the entire world. I think it’s a bad look for everyone involved. And we always want to be at Sports Illustrated in front of our fans when we earned that right throughout the season. But I would say it had no effect on performance today.” The match had been moved to Icahn on Monday due to concerns over the disintegrating field conditions at Sports Illustrated, which had unfortunately overshadowed Gotham’s quarterfinal victory there last weekend. Gotham was unbeaten in its past 13 matches at Sports Illustrated, which is operated by the Red Bulls of MLS. Croix Bethune, left, celebrates scoring a goal with Kansas City Current teammate Lo’eau LaBonta during an NWSL playoff match in New York, Nov. 15, 2026. Getty Images “I think that’s also part of the sadness,” head coach Juan Carlos Amorós said. “I think we never know what would have happened if we played on a good pitch. I think it was the right decision to come here. I think the pitch in the other stadium was unfortunately unplayable.” Tickets for the semifinal were reallotted and grabbed up in a hurry, while Gotham officials ground on the logistics of moving their game-day operations. “Obviously not ideal we had to change stadiums, but … I think that’s really awesome to come into a new environment, a new stadium, you have to adapt, you have to make sure you can bring that energy and our supporters did that tonight and that’s incredible,” Gotham midfielder Savannah McCaskill said. item.title: Beckham to be inducted into US Soccer Hall of Fame
item.description: David Beckham was knighted by King Charles in 2025 [Getty Images] David Beckham will be inducted into the United States' National Soccer Hall of Fame as part of its 2027 class. The former Manchester United and England midfielder, 51, made headlines in 2007 when he moved to Los Angeles from Spanish giants Real Madrid to join Major League Soccer (MLS) side LA Galaxy on a five-year contract. He made 124 appearances in all competitions for Galaxy, scoring 20 goals, and twice won both the MLS Cup and Supporters' Shield. Beckham's six seasons at Galaxy helped to raise the global profile of MLS and following his retirement in 2013, he became co-owner of MLS club Inter Miami, who signed Argentina World Cup winner Lionel Messi in 2023. His induction ceremony is set to take place on 16 April 2027 in Frisco, Texas. David Beckham's deal with LA Galaxy in 2007 was reportedly worth £128m [Getty Images] He was told the news he had been chosen on the veterans' ballot at an MLS board of governors' meeting on Thursday and said his time in the US has been "an incredible journey". Beckham, who had two loan spells with AC Milan in 2009 and 2010 while at Galaxy, added: "I'm looking to build this league and this sport in this great country for a long time." Meanwhile, former US internationals Megan Rapinoe and Julie Ertz have also been voted into the Hall of Fame in their first year of eligibility. Ballon d'Or winner Rapinoe, 41, and midfielder Ertz, 34, lifted the Women’s World Cup twice with with the US in 2015 and 2019. "To be alongside all the greatest players that have played for us, and played for our country alongside a bunch of my team-mates and friends, recognised like that in this way just means you were successful and a part of great teams," Rapinoe wrote on Instagram. item.title: Gotham FC’s home semifinal moved to 5K-seat stadium in field quality debacle
item.description: Seattle Reign FC defender Phoebe McClernon, left, defends Gotham FC forward Guro Reiten during an NWSL playoff game in Harrison, N.J., Sunday, Nov. 8, 2026. For the first time in franchise history, Gotham FC is set to host its semifinal match next weekend. But there’s an unfortunate twist. Gotham’s semifinal match against the Kansas City Current won’t be played at the club’s typical stomping grounds in Harrison, New Jersey. Instead, Gotham agreed to move Sunday’s match to Icahn Stadium on Randall’s Island for better playing surface quality. “This was an extremely difficult decision, and one we did not take lightly,” Gotham president of soccer operations Yael Averbuch West said in a letter to fans. “After thoughtful consultation with coach Juan Carlos Amorós, our team captains, and our ownership, we felt it was important to prioritize a playing surface that appropriately allows our athletes to perform at their best. Providing our players with a high-quality surface to compete is a responsibility we take very seriously.” The Gotham FC starting eleven line up before the NWSL playoff quarterfinal in Harrison, N.J., Sunday, Nov. 8, 2026. Lev Radin/Shutterstock Gotham is a tenant of Major League Soccer’s Red Bull New York at Sports Illustrated Stadium. The Red Bulls are scheduled to play an exhibition game there Saturday night, exacerbating concerns about the field quality. The state of Sports Illustrated Stadium’s pitch has been a cause for concern over the past two weeks. ESPN reported the NWSL fined Gotham $10,000 for poor field conditions during last week’s regular-season finale, after which the club was awarded its first league Shield. The pitch condition was once again a major sticking point after Gotham’s ugly quarterfinal win against the Seattle Reign. Retiring Reign midfielder Jess Fishlock called the field “atrocious.” Gotham defender Jess Carter was overheard saying the grounds were “so bad” when walking through the tunnel after the match. A week after Jaelin Howell injured her right ankle during a home game, the Gotham midfielder said the field was “pretty sandy” and “a little unstable.” Amorós acknowledged the rough conditions impacted the quality of the game. Seattle Reign FC defender Phoebe McClernon, left, defends Gotham FC forward Guro Reiten during an NWSL playoff game in Harrison, N.J., Sunday, Nov. 8, 2026. Corey Sipkin for the NY POST “At this level, in this kind of game, as a league, and we should have a better surface,” Amorós said. “Unfortunately, our club and football club did absolutely everything in their power to make sure that was the case. Unfortunately, it wasn’t. But luckily, it looks like nobody got hurt, and the game was what it was.” It’s not immediately clear if the NWSL penalized Gotham for a second consecutive week because of the field. item.title: NYCFC fires head coach Pascal Jansen after second-half collapse
item.description: NYCFC has fired head coach Pascal Jansen. New York City FC will be looking for a new head coach this offseason. Less than 24 hours after the club played its final match of the 2026 season, NYCFC announced that it fired head coach Pascal Jansen following a disappointing campaign that saw the club miss the playoffs for only the third time in its 12-year history. NYCFC went through an ugly 2026 season, finishing 11th in the Eastern Conference and being knocked out of playoff contention before the club even reached its Decision Day matchup with D.C. United on Saturday. The rough season was highlighted by the massive second-half collapse NYCFC went through following the World Cup break, posting a 5W-8D-6L record and sliding from eighth place to 11th. Jansen was informed of the decision by the club’s front office on Sunday morning and ultimately the decision to move on from him as head coach came down to the “failure of making playoffs” following a “disappointing season,” a source told The Post. NYCFC has fired head coach Pascal Jansen. Getty Images The head coaching role will take on an even bigger role going into 2027 as NYCFC prepares for massive changes with the planned move into their new stadium and MLS changing their league calendar to a summer-through-spring format, which is in line with the European football calendar and includes an abbreviated sprint season that will run from February to May. The club views this next year as a “crucial point in franchise history” and the feeling is that NYCFC wants to make sure it has “the right leadership in place,” the source added. NYCFC will begin its search for a new head coach immediately, sporting director Todd Dunivant said in a statement released late Sunday morning. “We would like to thank Pascal for his commitment and contributions to New York City FC and wish him and his family all the best. This decision follows a thorough review of the season and reflects our ambition as an organization,” he said. One of the biggest problems that NYCFC faced this season – especially during its struggles in the second half – had been allowing late goals that would cost the club points, or matches altogether. And the club dealt with a number of injuries during the course of the season, while also playing much of the year without one of its top scorers, Alonso Martinez, as he recovered from a torn ACL he suffered last fall. item.title: Messi makes history with MLS Golden Boot
item.description: Messi retired from international football with Argentina earlier this year [Getty Images] Inter Miami forward Lionel Messi has become the first player in MLS history to win the Golden Boot in consecutive seasons. The eight-time Ballon d'Or winner scored 26 goals in 31 appearances, four clear of FC Dallas striker Peter Musa and five more than Nashville's English forward Sam Surridge. Messi becomes only the sixth player to land the award twice, joining a list that includes former Charlton Athletic and Southampton striker Bradley Wright-Phillips. In addition to his goals, the 39-year-old notched 17 assists over the course of the MLS season, ensuring his 43 goal contributions was also a league best for the second year in a row. And the World Cup winner could soon make more history as he bids to become the first three-time Landon Donovan MLS MVP winner. The former Argentina forward landed the award in 2024 as Inter Miami won the Supporters' Shield title and also in 2025 as they won the MLS Cup. Despite Messi's magic, Miami weren't able to land top spot in the MLS Eastern Conference, with the team finishing 17 points behind Surridge's Nashville. They will now face Columbus Crew over three games in the first round of the MLS Cup play-offs which begin later this month. item.title: On MLS Decision Day, D.C. United faces a familiar reality: Another season of failure
item.description: WASHINGTON — All around Major League Soccer , from Montreal to Miami and Seattle to San Diego, Saturday was Decision Day — the last act in an 8½-month production. While three playoff berths were in the balance, teams with guaranteed spots sought to improve their place. It's a day marked by desperation, scoreboard-watching and playoff-planning. At Audi Field, however, Decision Day felt more like Derision Day. For the seventh consecutive year, D.C. United, once a showpiece of a blossoming league, has no playoff plans — a near impossibility in a league that distributes postseason passes like a guy on a New York street corner handing out flyers for discount mattresses. Only Toronto FC's eight-year rut, starting with its 2007 expansion campaign, lasted longer. United wasn't even in the mix on Decision Day, its fate having been decided 10 days earlier. The lowly finale was against another failed side, New York City FC, which claimed a 1-0 victory on a late goal. While 2026 was an anomaly for the New Yorkers, it was the norm in the nation's capital. D.C. added another sad chapter to a rotten story under an ownership group, led by Jason Levien and Steve Kaplan, that has dragged the organization into irrelevance in not just the prospering league but in the local market and the ascending sport. The public-address announcer introduces the team as "your four-time MLS Cup champions," but he's been saying that for a long time. Given the league's evolution, it feels even longer. United's last title, in 2004, came in a 10-team operation — one-third the current landscape. Since then, 13 different clubs have hoisted the trophy. Less than two miles north of Audi Field, the U.S. Capitol witnessed a historic sea change Tuesday with a political wave that swept the ruling party out of office. Local soccer fans have had no such luck with those in power at Audi Field. Under the current regime … United hasn't won a playoff game in 11 years and hasn't advanced to the conference finals in 14. Twelve years have passed since it won at least half its 34 matches. United's only trophy in recent memory was the 2013 U.S. Open Cup, which came amid a horrific, three-win regular season. D.C. is on its fourth head coach since Ben Olsen's departure in late 2020 and its second head of soccer operations in four years. The current director, Erkut Sogut — an agent best known for representing former German star Mesut Özil — was hired last fall without any experience working for a team. Another goal conceded, another season to forget. Keisuke Kurokawa's frustration summed up D.C. United's latest disappointing chapter. Scott Taetsch via Getty Images United remains one of three MLS organizations without a developmental team bridging the youth academy to the first team. Efforts to build a complex in Baltimore for an MLS Next Pro operation have floundered. (Meanwhile, United's owners have launched a pro volleyball team.)
